reuse.why: Wraps the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend in a new getOccurrenceAfterWeekendRule that all three weekend sites (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the schedule template loop) now call.

duplication.why: The weekend decision itself is no longer repeated at call sites; the remaining repetition is the 'daily needs extra candidates' heuristic restated in getNextDate (take 7) and getUpcomingDates (count * 7).

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside the recurrence helpers; only the over-fetch workaround for dropped occurrences leaks to callers instead of being expressed in the recurrence rule itself.

scope.why: Limited to the weekend rule, its three call sites and tests.

maintainability.why: One function owns the rule, but returning null for dropped dates forces magic candidate counts (7, count*7) and extra null-handling in the template loop, which a maintainer must keep consistent with the rule and which breaks for long daily intervals.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every former getDateWithSkippedWeekend caller now goes through getOccurrenceAfterWeekendRule, and getDateWithSkippedWeekend is made private.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated `frequency === 'daily'` over-fetch in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates is a visible small repetition, not disguised logic.

one_place.where: getOccurrenceAfterWeekendRule in shared/schedules.ts decides skip-vs-move from skipWeekend, frequency and weekendSolveMode, and getNextDate, getUpcomingDates (schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (budget/schedule-template.ts) all use it.
